title: Development of a Minimal Auxiliary Basis for the Particle--Particle Random Phase Approximation (ppRPA): Accelerating Excited-State Calculations in Diradical Nanoparticles and Periodic Systems
abstract:
arXiv:2610.18020v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Singlet--triplet gaps set the energy scale of the two-spin manifold in molecular quantum information materials, and such systems frequently carry diradical character: metal nanoclusters, metal--organic frameworks with radical linkers, and the nitrogen--vacancy center in diamond. Time-dependent density functional theory is the standard tool at this size but describes multireference systems poorly. A closed-shell reference is inadequate for a multiconfigurational ground state, and the adiabatic kernel excludes doubly excited configurations. The particle--particle random phase approximation (\pprpa{}) changes the particle number rather than the spin. Singlet and triplet states descend from one closed-shell reference, and double excitations enter on the same footing as single ones. Computational cost has confined \pprpa{} to small systems, and the two-electron integrals that drive it are factorized through an auxiliary basis. We develop \pprpa{}--as, which reduces that basis to a minimal set of atom-centered Gaussian shells whose exponents follow from free-atom radii and one global scaling factor. The approximation enters only the excited-state step, so both calculations proceed from the same self-consistent reference. We test molecules and clusters of up to 286 atoms, including heavy elements, and seven point defects in four periodic hosts, obtaining both multiplicities and their splitting without symmetry breaking or spin projection. We optimize the scaling factor and give guidance on choosing it. An order-of-magnitude smaller auxiliary basis delivers a speed-up of up to eightfold while staying within $0.03$~eV of conventional \pprpa{}, bringing diradical nanoclusters and periodic systems within reach.
relevance_reason: Develops a minimal auxiliary basis (ppRPA-as) to accelerate particle-particle RPA excited-state calculations for molecules, clusters, and periodic defects, satisfying (a) explicit atoms, (b) post-HF/electronic-structure method development, and (c) method advance.

title: First-fracture kinetics in periodic chains: from free-energy landscapes and dynamical recrossing to absolute rates
abstract:
arXiv:2610.16944v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: The nearly collinear configuration of highly stretched polymer chains before fracture motivates one-dimensional models. At fixed extension, stretching one bond redistributes length among the others, coupling rupture to the whole chain. In this work, I develop a framework for fracture-healing rates in periodic Morse chains, combining deterministic theories, equilibrium simulations and a quasi-deterministic approach using equilibrium fluxes and barrier-top trajectories. Constrained-partition calculations closely reproduce simulated populations and intact-state tensions. An intact-reservoir potential of mean force (PMF) supplies the first-fracture surface probability, while recrossing corrects the attempt flux without a rate-fitted prefactor. Independent rate tests identify an operational chain-length boundary for accurate two-state kinetics; failed-return durations decrease relative to population relaxation as chains grow. Kramers-Grote-Hynes (KGH), nonlinear reactive-flux and equilibrium rates show excellent agreement in this regime. KGH predicts rates away from coexistence and a chain-dependent local activation length dominated by the barrier response. Rates decrease approximately exponentially before declining more gently for longer chains: barrier growth dominates, additional fracture sites partly compensate, and transmission varies more weakly. Beyond coexistence, long chains can fracture practically irreversibly because healing becomes too rare to observe. Projected committor crossings, where the configuration-averaged probability of reaching the fractured core first is one half, lie near site-PMF maxima, although configurations at equal bond length retain different fracture probabilities. Multiple fractures remain negligible near coexistence through at least $N=50$. The framework could supply state-dependent rates to mesoscopic fracture models of polymer networks.
relevance_reason: Classical equilibrium and quasi-deterministic MD simulations of periodic Morse chains combined with constrained-partition free-energy/PMF and reactive-flux rate calculations, clearly satisfying (a)-(c) through MD and free-energy methodology.

title: pANO-F12: An atomic natural orbital-inspired route to more compact basis sets for F12 explicitly correlated methods
abstract:
arXiv:2605.22543v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Explicitly correlated methods such as MP2-F12 and CCSD(F12*) exhibit much faster basis set convergence (asymptotically $\propto L^{-7}$, with L the highest angular momentum) than orbital-only approaches. Yet it has been pointed out that cc-pVnZ-F12 basis sets themselves are substantially larger than the corresponding cc-pVnZ, and specifically that cc-pVDZ-F12 is the size of cc-pVTZ. One way to generate compact basis sets in an orbital-only context are Atomic Natural Orbital (ANO) basis sets [J. Alml\"of and P. R. Taylor, JCP 86, 4070 (1987)]. However, obtaining the required first-order reduced density matrix while properly accounting for the F12 geminal is problematic. In this work, we show that an energy minimization-based contraction process under linear independence constraints yields `pseudo-ANO' (pANO) basis sets that are functionally equivalent in quality. Subsequently, we apply this recipe to obtain pANO-F12 basis sets from the same elements, then validate them for several thermochemical benchmarks and for the hypersensitive out-of-plane vibrations of benzene. We show that, unlike cc-pVnZ-F12, pANO-F12 exhibits the familiar shell structure seen in cc-pVnZ and ANO basis sets, and that pANO-F12 offers a route to more compact F12 basis sets more amenable to medium-sized systems, especially in conjunction with localized pair natural orbital approaches. Overall, the pANO approach is most beneficial for the smaller double-and triple-zeta basis sets, offering either superior performance to cc-pVnZ-F12 at same cost, or similar performance at lower cost.
relevance_reason: Develops compact 'pseudo-ANO' basis sets for explicitly correlated post-Hartree-Fock methods (MP2-F12, CCSD(F12*)) validated on thermochemical benchmarks, satisfying (b) post-HF method development on explicit atomic systems (a) and (c) advancing quantum-chemistry methodology.

title: Role of defect trapping in the enhanced corrosion resistance of Ni-Mo alloys with yttrium and yttrium oxide additions
abstract:
arXiv:2610.15089v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Corrosion of structural alloys remains a critical challenge for advanced molten salt reactors, where aggressive fluoride salts promote continuous dissolution at the salt-metal interface. While most mitigation strategies emphasize thermodynamic stability, kinetic control of atomic transport has received comparatively less attention. Here, we propose a corrosion mitigation strategy based on diffusion control and vacancy trapping by dilute yttrium (Y) solutes and yttrium oxide (Y$_2$O$_3$) dispersions in Ni alloys. A combined computational and experimental approach integrates density functional theory (DFT), self-consistent mean-field (SCMF) diffusion modeling, and an impurity trapping model to quantify the impact of defect trapping on effective vacancy mobility. Strong first-nearest-neighbor vacancy-Y binding, off-lattice vacancy configurations, and elevated rotational and dissociation barriers result in pronounced suppression of vacancy diffusivity, while Y$_2$O$_3$-associated sites treated as fixed traps in the model further reduce the mobile vacancy population. Ni-Mo (NM), Y-modified (NMY), and Y$_2$O$_3$-containing (NMYO) alloys were tested in molten fluoride salt at 750{\deg}C. Corrosion penetration decreases systematically from NM to NMY to NMYO, consistent with the predicted reduction in vacancy-mediated transport. The same trend is observed in mass change, with net weight loss decreasing from 0.52% for NM to 0.23% for NMY and 0.09% for NMYO. These results are consistent with an alloy-side transport contribution from defect trapping and reduced atomic transport. This study therefore suggests point defect engineering as a promising alloy design strategy for extreme nuclear environments.
relevance_reason: DFT calculations of vacancy-Y binding, off-lattice configurations and migration barriers combined with self-consistent mean-field diffusion modeling satisfy (a) explicit atoms, (b) DFT/diffusion methodology, and (c) application to a real alloy corrosion problem.

title: Exact Symmetry as Algebra: Group-Structured Tensors that Enforce Physical Selection Rules
abstract:
arXiv:2605.20440v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Symmetry determines which physical responses of molecules and crystals are allowed and underlies many models used throughout the physical sciences. Yet several widely used machine-learned models learn symmetry only approximately from data, raising the question of whether approximate symmetry is sufficient for scientific prediction. Using the Orb-v3 force field, we show that it is often not: the relaxed space group of a crystal depends on the orientation of the input for $47\%$ of a $150$-crystal subsample, and relaxation lowers the space group for half of all $399$ crystals studied. To characterize, quantify, and correct such failures, we introduce a tensor algebra, $\star_G$, defined by convolution over a finite symmetry group and applicable to tensors with noncommuting entries. We prove that the symmetry group determines the algebra's block-diagonal transform and use this structure to analyze model errors on symmetric targets. The resulting projections decompose the average squared error into orthogonal components arising from selection-rule violations, inconsistencies across symmetry-related inputs, and residual error. The removable components reveal how much error arises from broken symmetry, provide reference-free lower bounds on prediction error, and can be eliminated without sacrificing accuracy. For operators, projection followed by blockwise truncation yields the optimal symmetric low-rank approximation. Applying these projections to force predictions reduces both rates of space-group change to at most $2\%$. Exact selection rules, reference-free error bounds, and symmetry-preserving corrections are therefore available for any trained model without retraining.
relevance_reason: Introduces a group-convolution tensor algebra for exact symmetry and demonstrates it on Orb-v3 MLIP crystal relaxations; (a) explicit atoms in crystals, (b) MLIP-driven geometry optimization, and (c) method advance for force fields are all satisfied.

title: A grand potential for molten-salt electrochemical phase diagrams from first principles
abstract:
arXiv:2610.17611v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: The clean-energy transition is driving unprecedented demand for metals, whose extraction is among the largest industrial sources of carbon emissions. Molten-salt electrolysis offers a path toward carbon-free production of aluminum, iron, titanium, and critical metals. However, corrosive operating conditions and complex, multicomponent feedstocks make experimental development costly and challenging. Here, we introduce a first-principles framework for constructing electrochemical phase diagrams of multicomponent systems to accelerate electrode and electrolyte design and guide the selection of compatible materials and operating conditions for electrochemical cells. We derive a grand potential that generates these diagrams at scale, and supply free energies using first-principles data obtained through a fine-tuned foundation machine-learned interatomic potential. For silicon in molten CaCl$_2$, the construction not only recovers the experimental diagram when using the first-principles framework on a limited set of structures, but also predicts further domains when extended to a larger set of crystal structures. Finally, we demonstrate the predictive power of the approach by screening ten alkali and alkaline-earth halide electrolytes for aluminum electrowinning. Three thermodynamic criteria identify NaF, where cryolite emerges as the stable aluminum-bearing phase, recovering the chemistry that Hall and H\'eroult established empirically in 1886. The framework provides a first-principles basis for selecting compatible electrodes, electrolytes, and operating conditions toward low-carbon metal production from complex source materials.
relevance_reason: Builds first-principles electrochemical phase diagrams for molten salts using free energies from a fine-tuned foundation MLIP on explicit crystal structures, satisfying (a)-(c) via MLIP/DFT-based atomistic energetics, though it constructs thermodynamic diagrams rather than running dynamics.

title: Vibrational Fingerprints of Competing Structural and Polar Phases in CuInP2S6
abstract:
arXiv:2610.16091v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Layered van der Waals CuInP2S6 crystals exhibit a rich sequence of temperature- and pressure-driven phase transitions, giving rise to multiple structural phases with distinct physical properties. Despite extensive experimental and theoretical efforts, unambiguous identification of these phases remains challenging because of their structural similarities and complex vibrational responses. In this work, we employ first-principles density functional theory calculations to systematically investigate the vibrational properties of the reference paraelectric C2/c and P-31c phases and their corresponding dynamically stable ferroelectric Cc and P31c phases, as well as the antiferroelectric P-1 and P-3 phases. From calculated phonon spectra and symmetry analysis, we determine the Raman- and infrared-active modes of each candidate structure and identify characteristic vibrational fingerprints that enable their phase determination through vibrational spectroscopy. Furthermore, using Porto notation, we establish polarization- and crystal-orientation-dependent Raman selection rules for different backscattering geometries and identify the modes that are expected to emerge or vanish under specific experimental configurations. Thus, our results provide a comprehensive theoretical framework for interpreting Raman and infrared measurements of CuInP2S6 and for reliably identifying its competing structural, ferroelectric, and antiferroelectric phases across temperature- and pressure-driven phase transitions.
relevance_reason: First-principles DFT calculations of phonon spectra and vibrational fingerprints on explicit CuInP2S6 crystal structures satisfy (a), (b) DFT methodology, and (c) application to real material phase identification.

title: Building new non-empirical hybrid and double-hybrid density functionals from the TCA family of GGA expressions
abstract: The Tognetti–Cortona–Adamo (TCA) correlation functional, and their subsequent variants, constitutes an important family of nonempirical generalized gradient approximations that have found successful applications in molecular and solid-state electronic structure calculations. In this work, we present a systematic assessment of the original TCA functional together with the revTCA, gracTCA, and transTCA variants within nonempirical hybrid (TCA0) and double-hybrid (TCA-QIDH) frameworks. Their performance is evaluated using the comprehensive GMTKN55 benchmark database, including more detailed analysis of the challenging MB16-43 and SIE4x4 subsets, as well as three different global performance metrics: WTMAD-2A, WTMAD-2B, and the recently proposed WTMAD-4. The results reveal a consistent improvement in accuracy upon ascending “Jacob’s ladder,” with the nonempirical double-hybrid models reducing the global errors by approximately a factor of 2–3 relative to their GGA counterparts. Among the semilocal functionals, the original TCA correlation provides the most balanced overall performance, while the differences among the various TCA-based models become much less pronounced at the double-hybrid level. Importantly, the relative ranking of the functionals is essentially unaffected by the choice of the WTMAD metric, demonstrating the robustness of the conclusions with respect to the weighting scheme adopted for the GMTKN55 database. The remaining deficiencies are associated with dispersion-dominated intermolecular interactions, highlighting the potential use of some long-range correlation corrections. Overall, this study confirms that the TCA functional, particularly when adopted in a double-hybrid scheme, constitutes a reliable and transferable framework for the development of accurate density functional approximations applicable to a broad range of chemical problems.
relevance_reason: Non-empirical hybrid and double-hybrid DFT functional development and benchmarking on molecular systems; explicit atoms (a), DFT methodology (b), and method advance (c) are all satisfied.
